origin: Post-hoc hypotheses generated from the already-open EOG Azores endpoint; same-data tests are exploratory.

eog_result.mechanism_boundary: The source study reports zero valid receiver-to-receiver movements, so the EOG gain is not evidence of dispersal.

primary_question: In a strongly resident island-stream eel population, is temporal predictability primarily an observation-system phenomenon, shared hydrological synchrony, or persistent local activity state?

mandatory_first_audit.name: receiver_operability
mandatory_first_audit.known_event: station 4 / 151 FLO CRUZ ceased detections after 2022-07-24 because of sediment burial
mandatory_first_audit.prediction: censoring known receiver failure changes the apparent temporal-memory signal
mandatory_first_audit.next_test: M0b vs M0 before any biological interpretation

hypotheses.name: persistent_residence_time_varying_detection
hypotheses.prediction: detections disappear and return at the same receiver; latent residence remains high while observation probability varies

hypotheses.name: shared_hydrological_synchrony
hypotheses.prediction: cross-pool temporal covariance attenuates after frozen rainfall/flow covariates

hypotheses.name: persistent_local_activity_regime
hypotheses.prediction: receiver/tag latent state remains persistent after receiver-operability and hydrology controls

not_primary: movement_compression is a later independent comparative hypothesis, not the explanation of the EOG residual in this zero-between-receiver-movement dataset
